title: Structural and cyclical budget parts
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers splitting the budget into structural and cyclical parts; fiscal policy and output gaps are related ideas, but neither teaches this distinction.

draft.title: Structural and cyclical budget parts
card: The budget balance can be split into two parts. Each part has a different cause.

the part of the balance that moves with the business cycle. In a downturn, tax revenue falls and welfare spending rises, which pushes the balance towards deficit. In a boom, the effect runs the other way.
the part of the balance that reflects the government's policy choices, such as tax rates and spending programs. It is what the balance would be if the economy were at its normal level of activity.
A deficit caused by a downturn is mostly cyclical, so it can shrink as the economy recovers. A deficit that remains when the economy is at its normal level of activity is structural.
draft.remember: Cyclical follows the economy. Structural follows government choices.

a.q: A recession cuts company tax revenue and raises unemployment payments, with no change to any tax rate or program. Which part of the budget balance has moved?
opts: Both parts by the same amount
Neither part, as policy did not change
a.why: The balance moved because the business cycle changed revenue and spending. That is the cyclical part. The structural part reflects policy choices, and none were made here, but this does not mean the balance stayed the same.
a.clue: What caused the change: the cycle or a policy decision?

b.q: Treasury finds the budget is in deficit even though the economy is at its normal level of activity. What does this suggest about the deficit?
opts: It is structural, reflecting policy settings
It is cyclical, and will close as growth returns
It is caused by the downturn in the business cycle
It is neither structural nor cyclical
b.why: At a normal level of activity the cycle adds little to the balance. A deficit that remains reflects the government's tax and spending choices, so it is structural. A cyclical deficit would be expected to shrink as the economy recovers, but here there is no downturn to recover from.
b.clue: Think about what is left once the cycle has no effect.

b.best: It is structural, reflecting policy settings
